sources.entry: TimeTracker - Track time across projects and clients, with timers, kanban tasks, CRM, expense tracking, multi-currency invoicing (PDF, Peppol/ZugFerd e-invoicing), reports, OIDC/SSO, and a REST API. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted, web-based time tracker for freelancers and teams that adds invoicing, expenses, CRM, and Peppol/ZUGFeRD e-invoicing, distributed as a Docker deployment.
summary.what_it_does: TimeTracker provides server-side timers that keep running after the browser closes, along with manual time entry, bulk entry, templates, a calendar view, and time rounding. Projects, tasks, and clients are managed through a Kanban board, issue tracking, and comments. Invoices can be generated from tracked time, with PDF export, tax calculation, multi-currency support, and e-invoicing via Peppol and Factur-X/ZUGFeRD XML embedded in PDFs. The app also covers expenses, mileage, payments, budgets, a CRM with a sales pipeline and lead scoring, and reports with CSV and PDF export. Access control includes role-based permissions, username-only login or OIDC/SSO, and API tokens for a REST API. An optional AI helper can run through a bundled Ollama service or an OpenAI-compatible provider, and the README also mentions Flutter and Electron apps and a Prometheus/Grafana monitoring stack.
use_cases: track billable hours across client projects
generate and send invoices from logged time
self-host time tracking on a NAS or Raspberry Pi
manage a small team's projects and tasks
track expenses and mileage alongside time
how_to_run: Open http://<host>:8080 and create the admin account on first login
notable: Peppol and EN 16931 e-invoicing via a bundled Peppol Bridge, with Factur-X/ZUGFeRD XML embedded in PDFs
Timers run server-side and persist across browser sessions
No per-user pricing; GPL-3.0 with features not gated behind a paywall
Optional AI helper that is off by default and can use a bundled Ollama or a hosted OpenAI-compatible API
Encryption at rest for stored secrets via a Fernet key
caveats: SQLite is documented only for testing and is not recommended for production
Recommended resources are 2GB+ RAM for Docker, and 4GB+ for production with 5+ users
The bundled Ollama option downloads a roughly 4.7 GB model by default and is opt-in
Some features (Peppol native sending, PDF/A-3 with veraPDF) are described in setup guides the README links to but not detailed here
